office_does: The sheriff runs the Pacific County Sheriff's Office, the county's law enforcement agency covering more than 1,200 square miles; since 2025 the jail has been a separate county department.
race_blurb: First-term Sheriff Daniel Garcia (Prefers Republican Party), a Navy veteran elected in 2022 without prior police experience, faces Rich Byrd (Prefers Independent Party), a retired lieutenant with 20 years in the office. They split over the drug task force Garcia let lapse, 24-hour coverage and whether the office needs more money.

candidates.summary: Incumbent sheriff since 2023 and retired Navy Reserve senior chief, running on rebuilding the office's detectives, search and rescue and training.
highlights: Says his office re-established a detective division, search and rescue team and internal affairs unit [S3][S4]
Let the county drug task force end by not seeking more state funding; says the sheriff's office now handles its cases [S4]
Says more deputies are needed but opposes raising taxes and did not support a 0.1% sales tax increase [S5]
Opposed the state law setting minimum experience standards for sheriffs [S6]
Fired his primary rival, deputy Sean Eastham, in August 2026 after an investigation [S9]

experience.basis: Incumbent running on his first-term record, but came to the office in 2023 from outside law enforcement.

taxes.basis: Says he opposes raising taxes and declined to support a proposed one-tenth of one percent sales tax increase.

safety.basis: Enforcement-led record (detectives, major cases solved) alongside co-responder crisis work.

spending.basis: Says the office needs more deputies but would manage without new tax revenue.

candidates.summary: Retired sheriff's lieutenant with about 20 years in the office and later a private-sector manager, running on restoring the drug task force and doing more with the current budget.
highlights: Would restore the drug task force 'day one' and rebuild dedicated drug enforcement [S5][S4]
Says the office budget doubled to $3.2 million under Garcia and 'we have to do better with what we have' [S6]
Would cut administrators' overtime and flex time to keep 24-hour coverage at both ends of the county [S5][S6]
Supports expanding designated crisis responders to seven days and co-responder programs [S4]

experience.basis: Challenger who has not held elected office; long career in the same office but out of law enforcement since 2010-2011.

spending.basis: Argues the office has enough money, calls requests for more 'ludicrous', and would cut overtime and redeploy administrators.

safety.basis: Enforcement-led drug strategy (task force, arrests of traffickers) paired with treatment access and expanded crisis responders.
